readsAs: a stick figure with raised arms, the stock 'community/charity' person icon
an orange sun or ball held in a cupped V, like hands or a valley
a clean navy-and-orange geometric sans wordmark with one special letter
judge.why: The held-sun V is a sensible idea that scales cleanly and avoids every banned cliché, but it slips into the generic raised-arms people icon, the angular flat-bottomed v clashes with the soft rounded letters around it, and navy with orange feels more like a utility than a warm neighbourhood co-op.

readsAs: orange disc with a signal/broadcast ripple in the corner
eye or target peeking out of a ball
judge.why: The warm, solid disc avoids corporate green and holds up in one colour, but the nested arcs read first as a wifi or podcast signal, not shared solar ownership, the cut-off top edge looks unresolved, and the detail turns to mush at 16–24px.

readsAs: generic person/user icon (orange head over a navy swoosh body)
sun setting into a cupped hand or valley curve
judge.why: The plain disc avoids the banned sun-with-rays cliché and holds up well from 16 px to 256 px, but the dot-over-swoosh shape reads first as the stock 'community/person' clip-art used by countless healthcare and HR brands; the curve doesn't read clearly as an S, and its knobbed, uneven terminals look unresolved rather than ownable.

readsAs: a chunky rounded wordmark with one orange letter swapped in as a filled bowl, like a sun sinking into a valley
the standalone symbol reads as a notched block over a smile curve, like a toilet, a monitor on a stand or a cartoon face
a friendly startup or delivery-app logotype
judge.why: The orange sunk-in 'u' gives the wordmark warm, neighbourly charm without corporate-green clichés, but the extracted icon adds a smile bar the wordmark doesn't have, reads as an odd fixture or face rather than sun-in-valley, and fills up into a blob below 32px, so the system isn't app-ready.
